beats.text: Every single time Cursor or Claude writes code for you, your GPU wastes up to 70% of its compute doing nothing.
beats.visual_focus: A 3D skyscraper model where individual floors flicker and vanish, causing the entire structure to tilt and buckle under its own weight.

beats.text: Standard methods use local, closed-form heuristics to prune weights. They treat each layer like an isolated island, blind to the catastrophic error propagation downstream.
beats.visual_focus: A chain of dominoes where each one is slightly misaligned, showing the error compounding exponentially as it travels through the network layers.

beats.text: Enter Learnable Subspace Projections. Instead of guessing, we assign an orthogonal projector to each layer, optimizing them end-to-end against the global KL divergence.
beats.visual_focus: A neural network layer being transformed by an orthogonal projection matrix, mapping high-dimensional activations into a refined, compressed latent subspace.

beats.text: We re-parameterize the layers by decomposing weights using SVD, keeping only the top-k singular vectors, and training the projectors to preserve the output distribution.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: The hook was actually sick—the skyscraper analogy hit hard because I hate how current pruning methods just break models. I stayed for the first half, but you lost me at 'orthogonal projector.' I know what SVD is from my linear algebra class, but you didn't explain why the projector is better than just standard weight pruning. It felt like you were just throwing math terms at me to sound smart instead of explaining the 'why'.
